headline: Sensex Soars Over 1,500 Points as Nifty Reclaims 25,800 Driven by Foreign Fund Inflows

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Strong foreign fund inflows and foreign institutional investor (FII) buying.
Lower global crude oil prices boosting investor sentiment.
Rally led by FMCG and private banking sectors.
Support from reverse AI trade helping Indian markets recoup 2026 losses.
whatHappening: BSE Sensex surged over 1,500 points while Nifty 50 crossed the 25,800 mark.
The US proposed a fresh set of levies including 17% tariffs on India across 14 trading partners.
India's net FDI dropped to a 5.5-year low in September 2026 as outflows surged 40%.
Government permitted duty-free raw sugar imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes through March 2027.
summary: Indian stock markets staged a massive rally on November 25, 2026, with the Sensex surging over 1,500 points and Nifty crossing 25,800. The sharp upturn was powered by foreign fund buying, lower crude oil prices, and gains in private banks and FMCG stocks. Despite the market gains, macro concerns persisted with new US tariff proposals and falling FDI figures.
